method.summary: Start, finish, stops and pace of every driver.
steps: Start position = a driver's first position sample; finish = the last sample.
Stops = number of tyre stints - 1.
Lap statistics use the clean laps:
Start from the laps that passed validation.
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits: cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back time gained as fuel burns off).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x the driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents and safety-car laps).
method.formula: gained = start - finish;  lap_std = standard deviation of clean lap times;  avg_delta_field = mean(adjusted time - median adjusted time of all clean laps)
method.baseline: Field median pace for the delta; otherwise none.
assumptions: The fuel correction (0.03 s per lap) is an assumption, not a measurement.
limitations: Finish is the last live position sample, not the official classification (penalties are not reflected).
There is no separate safety-car detection: safety-car laps are only removed by the slow-lap rule.

method.summary: Race position at the start of each lap.
steps: For each lap take the position sample nearest to the lap's start time.
method.formula: position(driver, lap) = nearest position sample to lap.date_start
limitations: A position change inside a lap shows on the next lap.

method.summary: Clean lap time of every driver.
steps: Start from the laps that passed validation.
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits: cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back time gained as fuel burns off).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x the driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents and safety-car laps).
method.formula: plotted value = real lap time in seconds (not the fuel-adjusted time)
assumptions: The fuel correction (0.03 s per lap) is an assumption, not a measurement.
limitations: There is no separate safety-car detection: safety-car laps are only removed by the slow-lap rule.

steps: One bar per stint from lap_start - 1 to lap_end.
Remove stops of 40.0 s or more (repairs / red-flag stops).
method.formula: plotted value = pit-lane time in seconds
limitations: Pit-lane time only, not the total race time lost.

method.summary: How much slower the car gets as the tyres age, per compound.
steps: Start from the laps that passed validation.
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits: cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back time gained as fuel burns off).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x the driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents and safety-car laps).
Tyre age = age at stint start + lap - stint start lap + 1.
Keep ages up to 35.
delta = adjusted time - driver's median adjusted time.
Average delta per (compound, age); keep points with >= 3 laps and compounds with >= 4 ages.
method.formula: degradation(compound, age) = mean(adjusted time - driver's median adjusted time)
assumptions: The fuel correction (0.03 s per lap) is an assumption, not a measurement.
limitations: The track gets faster during a race, which flatters old tyres.
There is no separate safety-car detection: safety-car laps are only removed by the slow-lap rule.

method.summary: Track and air temperature during the session.
steps: No filtering beyond validation.
limitations: One weather station, about one sample a minute.

charts.title: Pace vs field and vs teammate

method.summary: A driver's clean pace compared with the field and with their teammate, lap by lap.
steps: Start from the laps that passed validation.
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits: cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back time gained as fuel burns off).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x the driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents and safety-car laps).
delta vs field = adjusted time - median adjusted time of all clean laps.
delta vs teammate = adjusted time - teammate's adjusted time on the same lap.
method.formula: delta_field = adj - median(adj, all clean laps);  delta_teammate = adj - adj_teammate(lap)
method.baseline: Field median / the teammate. Negative = faster.
assumptions: The fuel correction (0.03 s per lap) is an assumption, not a measurement.
limitations: The field median mixes different tyre ages and fuel loads.

method.summary: Every lap of the driver, including removed ones.
steps: Nothing is hidden: 'status' is 'clean' or the cleaning rule that removed the lap.
method.formula: status = clean, or the id of the rule the lap failed

steps: Start from the laps that passed validation.
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits: cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back time gained as fuel burns off).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x the driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents and safety-car laps).
avg pace = mean clean lap time in the stint.
degradation = slope of a straight line fitted to (tyre age, adjusted time); needs >= 5 clean laps.
method.formula: degradation = slope of the least-squares fit  adj_time ~ tyre_age
assumptions: The fuel correction (0.03 s per lap) is an assumption, not a measurement.
limitations: A straight line cannot show a tyre 'cliff'.

method.summary: Car positions on the circuit, scrubbable through the race.
steps: Location was thinned when downloaded: one sample per driver every 2.0 s.
Samples with x = y = z = 0 are removed (invalid frames).
All drivers are placed on one clock (seconds since session start) by linear interpolation; before a driver's first / after their last sample no dot is drawn.
The outline is one driver's clean lap drawn through its own samples.
The running order comes from the position table, not from where the dots are on the drawing.
method.formula: x(t), y(t) = linear interpolation between the two nearest samples of that driver
limitations: Sampling is coarse, so the outline is polygonal.
'Received' location rows are counted after thinning.
